answer: To bind a ENS domain to an agent, the registry runs a timestamped expiring signature. The owner signs a challenge stamped with the current time, valid only for a short window, and the registry verifies the response before recording the link. The relic of the check is the signature itself; a pearl in the response invalidates the claim, and a signal of mismatched links is rejected, so a Sybil cannot borrow a ENS domain to multiply identities.
